clue.text: European smuggling one large, exploding cigar for James Bond

indicators.note: to smuggle something is to carry it hidden inside, so the first word holds the next
something exploding is blown apart, so the word after it is scattered into a new order

blocks.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the five letters of the smoke rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy-film scene: a European smuggler with a big cigar that blows up, a gadget fit for 007.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-and-large pair is split around the last letter of the European: one goes inside, large follows outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor played the fictional secret agent in five films from Casino Royale onwards, so the name stands for the role.

clue.text: Straighten out Geordie presenter, say, drinking litres

indicators.note: whatever is drinking takes something inside it, so the earlier words surround the next one

blocks.note: Declan Donnelly, the Dec of Ant and Dec, is a TV presenter from Newcastle, home of the Geordies
to utter is to say
L is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: A TV presenter from the North East needs sorting out after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne. DEC and UTTER together drink L: DEC(L)UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing away mess and clutter from a room is tidying or straightening it out.

clue.text: High-fliers who have become home-makers?

blocks.note: surface reading: ambitious career people who have given up work to look after a household
setter's reading: birds, literal high fliers, building a place to raise their young

explanation.surface: Ambitious career people who have swapped the office for keeping house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' suggests successful executives, but here it means birds, which literally make homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that build twiggy homes for eggs and chicks are called by a word for those who build such shelters.

clue.text: Unique cryptic clues, I’ve written over ten

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the words that follow are jumbled
letters written over something cover it, so they go around it

blocks.note: the seven letters of these words rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A setter boasting that their cryptic clues are one of a kind, ten of them written.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are wrapped around X: E(X)CLUSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exclusive is the only one of its kind, not shared with others, which is a sense of unique.

clue.text: Picked up perfumes for a little cash

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on the radio, so the sound of the next word matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: perfumes are scents, which is said the same as a word for small coins

explanation.surface: Someone collected perfumes that cost only a little money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar or euro, so several of them are a small sum of money.

clue.text: Fighter with degrees in Old Persian

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous boxer
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree; two of them for the plural

explanation.surface: A boxer with university degrees in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Persian' looks like a language you might take degrees in; it is the definition, the character from the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Forty Thieves tale in the Arabian Nights is a woodcutter from long-ago Persia.

clue.text: Clutch pot son knocked off piano

indicators.note: something knocked off is removed, so the named letter goes from the word

blocks.note: pot and grass are both slang for cannabis
S is the abbreviation for son
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone grips a pot while a boy knocks things off the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS loses one S, then P is added: GRAS + P.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch something is to seize it firmly with the hand, the same as to grasp it.

clue.text: Husband avoids surprises, getting unimaginative Christmas present?

indicators.note: when a letter avoids a word it stays out of it, so it is removed

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
shocks are surprises

explanation.surface: A husband avoids any surprises by getting the same dull Christmas gift as every year.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOCKS without its H leaves SOCKS. The question mark marks the definition as an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear in a box is the stereotypical uninspired festive gift, a standing joke about lazy present buying.

clue.text: Model can do her hair etc in lounge

blocks.note: to sit is to model, posing for an artist
a tin is a can
to groom is to tidy one's hair and appearance

explanation.surface: A model gets ready, doing her hair and so on, in the living room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person and 'can' as a verb in the surface; here they are a verb meaning pose and a noun meaning container.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge is the main room of a house for relaxing in, the room otherwise called by this name.

clue.text: Frank and Anthea regularly ignored job-seeker

indicators.note: every other letter is passed over at a steady interval, leaving the rest

blocks.note: frank and candid both mean honest and open
the first, third and fifth letters of the name

explanation.surface: Two people, Frank and Anthea, with one of them passed over for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a man's name beside Anthea, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone applying for a post, so a person seeking a job in a selection process.

clue.text: Where young Boris was strangely genteel and cool

indicators.note: something strangely arranged is out of its normal order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Young Boris was oddly refined and laid-back at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, former UK Prime Minister, was educated at this famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson attended this elite boys' boarding school near Windsor as a teenager, so it is where he was.

clue.text: Ex-PM of Germany invested in real gold

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so a letter goes into the word

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
real and true both mean genuine
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A former prime minister of Germany put money into real gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Germany' seems to say whose ex-PM this is, but Germany only supplies its vehicle code; the leader was Canadian.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin Trudeau, and his father Pierre before him, served as prime minister of Canada.

clue.text: Head cleaner in Post Office wearing fake ring

indicators.note: what is wearing something has it on the outside, so the later words wrap around the earlier

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: The chief cleaner at a post office wears a fake ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head cleaner' looks like a senior cleaner; it is something that cleans the head. SHAM and O wear PO: SHAM(PO)O.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is the liquid soap used for washing the hair and scalp, a cleaner for the head.

clue.text: Current postman’s periodically mislaid letters from abroad

indicators.note: letters lost at regular intervals leave every other one behind

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The current postman keeps losing mail sent from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from abroad' suggests foreign post; it means letters of a foreign alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so several of them are letters from a foreign script.

clue.text: Saccharine last ice-cream, somewhat hard

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of the run of words is used

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: The final ice-cream is sickly sweet and a bit too firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will not stretch or give is rigid and unyielding, which is one sense of hard.

clue.text: Daisy tucked into case of edible goods, a seasonal treat

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
something tucked into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters
the aster is a daisy-like flower
G is short for good, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A flower tucked into a box of food, a gift for a festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goods' gives two letters because G is the standard abbreviation for good, doubled to make a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are given and eaten each spring at the Christian festival, a treat tied to that time of year.

clue.text: US leader – rotter is about right! One in a powerful suit picking up tricks

definitions.text: One in a powerful suit picking up tricks

indicators.note: about means around, so the word goes round the next letter

blocks.note: Donald Trump, US president
a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly man
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A jibe that the US leader is a rotter, and a powerful man in a suit picking up tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful suit' and 'tricks' sound political; they are card-game terms. CAD goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: In whist and bridge a card of the trumps suit beats any other suit and wins the trick it is played to.

clue.text: People tending to beds collect small covers from Parisian

indicators.note: something that covers another goes over and around it

blocks.note: to garner is to gather or collect
de is French for from
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Hotel staff making beds gather small bedcovers from a Parisian supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests bedrooms; it means flowerbeds. GARNER and S cover DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who look after flower and vegetable plots in a garden are the people who tend beds.

clue.text: Rio ate first of curried stews – spicy stuff!

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken
stewing mixes ingredients up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: In Rio someone ate curry before stews, a fiery meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spicy' suggests hot food; here it means racy.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually suggestive writing or art, the sort of risqué material called spicy.

clue.text: Heartless Conservative left to admit regret

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so these letters take another word inside

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
rue means regret
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A heartless Conservative politician leaves rather than admit any regret.
explanation.walkthrough: C and L admit RUE between them. 'Heartless' suggests removing middle letters, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cruel has no compassion or pity, someone without feeling, as if lacking a heart.

clue.text: Performer who will take a big bow?

definitions.text: Performer who will take a big bow?

blocks.clueFragment: Performer who will take a big bow?
blocks.note: surface reading: an actor or singer taking a deep bow at curtain call

blocks.clueFragment: Performer who will take a big bow?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a musician who plays with a large bow drawn over strings

explanation.surface: A star performer bowing deeply to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface; it really rhymes with 'go', the stick strung with horsehair.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the large stringed instrument held between the knees uses a long bow, bigger than a violinist's.

clue.text: Speechifying from either a Labourite ____?

blocks.note: 'either' calls for 'or' in the gap, followed by the name for a member of Labour's chief rival party

explanation.surface: Grand speeches from a politician of one main party or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either' needs an 'or' to follow, and Labour's rival is the Tory party, so the gap is OR A TORY, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, especially in a grand style, which is what speechifying describes.

clue.text: King in a lot of pain – it’s gas

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
in places the first letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: agony is great pain
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king in great pain blames it on wind.
explanation.walkthrough: AGONY loses its Y to give AGON, and R goes inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, the inert element making up about one per cent of the air.

clue.text: The solver’s joy? Our setter welcomes it

indicators.note: the words before welcome the answer in, holding it inside their letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: The setter is pleased to give the solver a moment of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressed to the person solving, the possessive pronoun for 'belonging to you' means the solver's.

clue.text: Oval shape, different around rim

indicators.note: around places the first word so it surrounds the next

blocks.note: else means other, different
a lip is a rim, as of a cup

explanation.surface: An oval design that differs because of the edge around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a synonym, and 'around' is the real instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a regular oval curve, a flattened circle, so it is an oval shape in geometry.

clue.text: I’d augment bust size

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the words before it are broken up and remade

blocks.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers to enlarge their bust size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust size' looks like a measurement phrase; 'bust' is the signal to rearrange and 'size' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude is greatness of extent or amount, the bigness of something, which is its size.

clue.text: Concern of PR department that is saving publication

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so the first words hold the next one

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A PR department is worried about saving a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: IE holds MAG: I(MAG)E. PR is public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Public relations staff exist to manage how an organisation is perceived, its public reputation.

clue.text: Myopic prophet given a title, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: a prophet is a seer, and a man given the title Sir has been knighted; the K is silent, so the opening sounds are S and N

explanation.surface: A short-sighted prophet is honoured with a knighthood.
explanation.walkthrough: SEER KNIGHTED with its opening sounds swapped becomes NEAR SIGHTED; the K of KNIGHTED is silent, so the N sound moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the condition in which distant things look blurred, so a myopic person sees only close things clearly.
